description: We are Huiñaypaq Ccanhuan (“Always With You”), a team of Peruvian students using science and technology to improve healthcare. Through ASTRA, we aim to monitor astronauts’ vital signs and physiological patterns throughout their missions, helping identify changes and protect their well-being. Inspired by healthcare inequalities in Peru, we believe innovation must go beyond recognizing problems: it must help address them. Our mission is to use technology to care for people, wherever they are.
summary: ASTRA Physiological Monitoring is an interactive platform developed to monitor astronaut health during space missions by tracking vital signs, identifying unusual physiological changes, and detecting potential health risks. By bringing complex health data together in one accessible interface, ASTRA aims to support better-informed decisions and help protect astronauts during long-duration missions. Beyond space exploration, we see an opportunity to apply these same capabilities to healthcare on Earth. Peru faces significant challenges, including limited medical resources, unequal access to healthcare, and inefficiencies in patient monitoring. ASTRA draws inspiration from these needs, exploring how technology developed for space missions can also become an accessible and efficient tool for healthcare professionals in our own country.
details:
ASTRA's Monitoring Features

ASTRA is a physiological monitoring and decision-support platform designed to help astronauts monitor their health during space missions. Specifically:

  • Integrates key physiological indicators, including heart rate, HRV, SpO₂, respiratory rate, blood pressure, body temperature, sleep, and physical activity.
  • Establishes individual physiological baselines to identify unusual changes.
  • Analyzes multiple indicators to detect potentially concerning patterns.
  • Displays health trends, alerts, activity records, and simulated physiological anomalies through an interactive dashboard.

How ASTRA Works

ASTRA follows five main steps:

  1. Data Collection: Receives physiological information from wearable sensors. The current prototype uses simulated telemetry.
  2. Personalized Baselines: Establishes individual reference values to account for each astronaut's normal physiological patterns.
  3. Data Analysis: Uses rule-based logic to evaluate indicators and identify unusual changes.
  4. Risk Assessment: Assigns a colour-coded health status and generates visual alerts when potential concerns are detected.
  5. Visualization: Presents physiological trends, sleep, activity, and alerts through a centralized dashboard.

Benefits for Astronauts

  • Health Monitoring: Combines multiple physiological indicators in one interface.
  • Early Awareness: Highlights unusual changes and potentially concerning patterns.
  • Personalization: Evaluates physiological changes according to individual baselines.
  • Autonomy: Helps astronauts independently understand and monitor their health.
  • Adaptability: Provides a foundation for healthcare applications beyond space exploration.

ASTRA's Future in Peru

In the short term, we aim to improve the prototype, integrate real wearable sensors, and validate its monitoring and alert mechanisms.

In the long term, we envision adapting ASTRA for healthcare applications in Peru, including hospitals, rural clinics, ambulances, firefighters, police personnel, and research institutions.

This vision includes developing an affordable wearable wristband capable of collecting vital signs and transmitting them to a centralized platform. Although this hardware has not yet been developed, our ambition is to explore pilot applications within Peruvian healthcare institutions, particularly in communities with limited access to medical resources.

Tools & Technologies Used

  • Programming Languages: Python, HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript.
  • Development Environment: Visual Studio Code.
  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript.
  • Data Processing: Python and rule-based physiological assessment.
  • AI Assistance: Claude AI for debugging, code improvement, and interface development.
  • Research & Data Sources: NASA physiological research, scientific publications, and datasets including BEDREST0543.
  • Testing: Simulated physiological telemetry and anomaly scenarios.
  • Deployment & Version Control: GitHub Pages and GitHub.
  • Hardware: No physical hardware developed yet; wearable wristband proposed for future development.
